parts.t: Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.

Triangle B is reflected in the x‑axis to give triangle C.

the shape is the same way round

Triangle T has vertices (2, 2), (6, 2) and (2, 4).
Triangle T is enlarged by scale factor −1⁄2 with centre (0, 0) to give triangle U.

parts.t: Find the coordinates of the vertices of triangle U.

The area of triangle T is 4 square units.
Work out the area of triangle U.
Write down the scale factor of the enlargement, centre (0, 0), that maps triangle U onto triangle T.

sols: The centre is the origin, so multiply both coordinates of each vertex by −<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>.
(2, 2) → (−1, −1)
(6, 2) → (−3, −1)
(2, 4) → (−1, −2)
Vertices of U: (−1, −1), (−3, −1) and (−1, −2)
the negative sign turns the triangle through 180° about the origin
Areas are multiplied by the square of the scale factor.
(−<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> = <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>4</sub>
the square of a negative number is positive
Area of U = 4 × 1⁄4 = 1 square unit
Check: U has base 2 and height 1, and 1⁄2 × 2 × 1 = 1 ✓
The inverse of an enlargement of scale factor k is an enlargement of scale factor 1⁄k with the same centre.
1 ÷ (−1⁄2) = −2
check: (−1, −1) × (−2) = (2, 2) ✓
